info.title: Broadsheet API
info.summary: Follow feeds and read them as a newspaper.
info.description:
The REST contract under `/api`, following the [Zalando RESTful API Guidelines](https://opensource.zalando.com/restful-api-guidelines/) with the deviations in the `api-design` skill: JSON properties are snake_case, ids are opaque strings, timestamps are RFC 3339, and every error is `application/problem+json`.

Every operation needs a signed-in session (the `broadsheet_session` cookie set by the browser sign-in at `/auth/login`) and acts for that person, except the few marked `security: []`. Every query is scoped to the signed-in person, so another person's resource is a `404`. A request that changes something must come from the app's own pages: a cross-site request (`Sec-Fetch-Site` or `Origin` naming another site) is refused with `403`, while a client that sends neither header is not. Requests are rate limited by the platform, and a blocked request is answered with `429` and `Retry-After`.

Only the REST contract under `/api` is described here. Sign-in and sign-out flows (`/auth/*`), OAuth (`/oauth/*` and `/.well-known/*`), the MCP endpoint (`/mcp`), webhooks (`/webhooks/*`), server-sent events (`/events/*`), the image proxy (`/img`), feeds out (`/feed.xml`), CSP reports (`/csp/reports`) and the health check (`/health`) sit outside `/api` and are not part of this contract.

get.summary: Search the archive of articles from the feeds the person follows, or list the most read or saved.
get.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. Every edition is searched, newest article first (oldest first with `order=oldest`). Without `q` every article is listed. With a trending `order` the list is NewsBlur's: `reads` (well read) ranks by distinct readers then seconds spent, `read_time` by seconds spent in reads of three seconds or more, `long_reads` by the second-deepest read of a story of 600 words or more read through by two or more, `good_reads` by stories someone saved first and then the second-deepest read of 30 seconds or more on a story of 250 words or more (or four such readers), and `saves` by distinct savers. A story counts only once two or more people are behind it, so a count never points at one reader; only counts are shown, never who. The ranked list then shows each story once (by cluster and title), takes one story per feed, site and publisher and at most three of a topic in each block of twelve, and keeps any source to a tenth of the list. `q` and `feed_id` are refused with a trending order; the cursor is a place in the list.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Words every article must hold in its title, summary, text, author or tags. An `author:` or `tag:` term (quoted for several words, as `author:"Ada Lovelace"`) matches only that field, as NewsBlur's search does.

parameters.name: feed_id
parameters.description: Only articles from this one feed, newest first. A feed the person does not follow lists nothing. Not with a trending order.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: Newest or oldest first, or one of the trending rankings.

parameters.name: window
parameters.description: How far back reads or saves count. Only with a trending order.

parameters.name: read
parameters.description: `false` leaves out the stories the person has read. Only with a trending order.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: `oldest` serves a trending list from its end. Only with a trending order.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The opaque cursor from a previous page's `next`.

get.summary: Read one article with its text.
get.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. When the daily scrape did not fetch the article's text, it is fetched from the original page the first time it is asked for and kept; a page with less than 100 characters of text is kept as having none. An article from a source the person does not follow, or an id that cannot name one, is a 404.

get.summary: List the stories most like one article.
get.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. Stories that share the most words of the article's title, best first, never another copy of the same address. With `scope=followed` (the default), up to ten from the sources the person follows; with `scope=all` (discover), up to five from any source, each saying whether the person follows its source (follow one with `POST /api/feeds`). One page, with no `next`. An article from a source the person does not follow, or an id that cannot name one, is a 404.

post.summary: Fetch an article's text again from its page.
post.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. The text is kept on the article, replacing what was there; an extraction is not stored apart from it, so the answer is the article and the status 200. When the article has no picture, the page's lead picture becomes its picture. An article from a source the person does not follow, or an id that cannot name one, is a 404.

200.description: The article with its text as fetched now.

post.summary: Add a custom edition, a named paper with its own rules.
post.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. A section that is not the person's is a 400. The daily run lays out an issue of every edition.

patch.summary: Rename a custom edition or change its rules.
patch.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. Only the members sent are changed. An edition that is not the person's, or an id that cannot name one (such as `self`), is a 404.

200.description: The edition as it is now.

delete.summary: Remove a custom edition and the issues it printed.
delete.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. An edition that is not the person's, or an id that cannot name one (such as `self`), is a 404.

get.summary: Read the paper one of the person's custom editions printed on one day.
get.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. An edition that is not the person's, a day the daily run laid out no issue of it, or a date that is not a calendar date, is a 404.

get.summary: List the person's briefings, newest first.
get.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. Briefings are written on the person's schedule (see their preferences) and kept one per slot and local day.

post.summary: Write a briefing now, for the slot of the person's day they are in.
post.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. Calls Workers AI. Too few stories in the window is a 404.

200.description: The briefing, written again in place of that slot's.

get.summary: Read one of the person's briefings.
get.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding.

get.summary: List the papers the person was given, newest first.
get.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. `self` is the person's default edition.

post.summary: Lay one day's paper out again, with a fresh editor's note.
post.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. Writing the note calls Workers AI, unless the person turned the note off. A day the person has no edition for is a 404.

200.description: The day's issue, laid out again in place of the one stored.

201.description: The day's issue, laid out for the first time.

get.summary: Read the paper the person was given on one day.
get.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. `self` is the person's default edition. Issues are laid out by the daily run; a day it laid out none, or a date that is not a calendar date, is a 404.

post.summary: Ask a question about an article, answered from its text by Workers AI.
post.description: Rate limited by the `RL_AI` binding, and by a daily budget (`GET /api/users/self/usage`) answered with 429 and `Retry-After` until midnight UTC. Only articles from sources the person follows can be asked about; any other is a 404. A preset answer with no history is kept and served again (`cached`) without counting against the budget; the reader's own questions and follow-ups are not kept. Each model, and thinking, keeps its own cached answers. The answer is always JSON; streaming it as server-sent events is not part of this contract.

get.summary: The person's conversations, last active first, without their turns.
get.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding.

post.summary: Start a conversation with the archive assistant.
post.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. Takes no body.

201.description: The conversation, with no turns yet.

get.summary: Starter questions for the assistant.
get.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. Drawn from the sources the person reads most and the tags they save under; at most six, as one page.

get.summary: A conversation with its turns.
get.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. Another person's conversation is a 404.

delete.summary: Remove a conversation and its turns.
delete.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. Another person's conversation is a 404.

post.summary: Ask the archive assistant a question.
post.description: Rate limited by the `RL_AI` binding, and by a daily budget (`GET /api/users/self/usage`) answered with 429 and `Retry-After` until midnight UTC. The assistant searches the person's followed sources, saves and reads with tools (full-text search with a date range and source, saved stories by tag with their notes and highlights, a summary of the saves, stories readers shared with their comments, recent reads, one story in full, an archive summary) and cites the stories it used; it can cite only stories it was given. The first question titles the conversation. The question and the answer are both kept as turns; when the model fails nothing is kept.

Location.description: The conversation the answer was added to.

post.summary: Email a story to up to ten addresses.
post.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. Sent through Cloudflare Email Sending; answers 503 until it is set up on the server. Replies go to the sender, who gets a copy unless `copy_me` is false. Each person may email 32 stories a day; past that the answer is 429.

202.description: The mail service took the email.

get.summary: List the feeds the person follows, as JSON or OPML.
get.description: Answers JSON by default and OPML when the request sends `Accept` `text/x-opml`, with sections as folders. The OPML form is the whole list; the JSON form is a cursor page. Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding.

post.summary: Follow a feed.
post.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. The address may be a page, in which case the feed it declares or links to, or one at a usual path, is followed instead, and an address that is a page with no feed to be found is a 400. The first edition of a new feed is fetched in the background.

url.description: An http(s) address, at most 2048 characters.

200.description: The person already follows this address.

patch.summary: Rename, mute (for good or for a time), reorder or file a feed under a section.
patch.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. Only the members sent are changed. A `section_id` that is not one of the person's sections is a 400. An id that cannot name a feed is a 404. A new `url` is refused with 409 when the person already follows it.

200.description: The feed as it is now.

409.description: The person already follows a feed at the new `url`.

delete.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. An id that cannot name a feed is a 404.

204.description: The feed is no longer followed.

post.summary: Follow many feeds at once from an OPML file or from topics.
post.description: Folders in an OPML file become sections, nested folders nested sections (to 8 levels), as do the topics. A feed counts as already followed when its address (ignoring scheme, `www.` and a trailing slash) or its `htmlUrl` matches one the person follows, or when it carries the name (ignoring case) of one they follow. A feed's name from the file becomes the person's own name for it when the feed is known under another. Feeds already followed are skipped and invalid ones rejected, neither failing the request. A file of more than 50 feeds is followed in the background a chunk at a time, and the answer is then 202 with the import's progress, to be watched at its `Location` until `status` is no longer `running`. Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding.

schema.description: An OPML document of at most 1 MiB and 500 feeds. `text/xml` and `application/xml` are accepted too.

202.description: The import of a large file started.

Location.description: The import, to watch its progress.

413.description: The body is over the size limit.

get.summary: How far an import of feeds got.
get.description: The progress of one of the caller's imports and what it did so far. Finished imports are kept for a week. Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding.

post.summary: Fetch one feed again now, forgetting its failures.
post.description: The way out of a broken feed. A refresh is not stored, so the result is the response. Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding.

200.description: The feed fetched; its statistics as they are now.

502.description: The feed could not be fetched; the detail says why.

get.summary: How a feed is doing.
get.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. An id that cannot name a feed is a 404.

200.description: The feed's last fetch, last error, failures in a row and recent output.

get.summary: Sources like one of the person's feeds.
get.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. Sources that people who follow this feed's source also follow, and the person does not, most shared first, each with its newest headlines; five a page by default. Another person's feed is a 404.

get.summary: Trending sources.
get.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. After NewsBlur's trending sites. `popular` has the most followers; `rising` gained the most followers for its size in the window; `hidden` gems have at most 50 followers but the most reads and saves per follower in the window; `new` arrivals were first followed in the window. One page.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: popular (the default), rising, hidden or new.

parameters.name: days
parameters.description: The window, in days.

post.summary: Find the feed of an address, or build a Google News feed.
post.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. After NewsBlur's newsletter conversion and Google News feeds. Nothing is kept or followed; follow the result with `POST /api/feeds`.

get.summary: Feeds put forward for everyone.
get.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. Approved ones by default, last approved first; the first is the feed of the day. Listing `pending` or `declined` ones needs the curator capability (see the `session` security scheme); anyone else asking for them gets a 403. One page.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: approved (the default), pending or declined.

post.summary: Put a feed forward for everyone.
post.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. The recommendation waits for a curator.

patch.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. Approves or declines a recommendation. This needs the curator capability (see the `session` security scheme); anyone else gets a 403.

get.summary: Search podcasts, with their feeds.
get.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. Found by the iTunes Search API; podcasts without a feed are left out. One page.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: What to search for.

get.summary: The Google News topics a feed can follow.
get.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. Use an `id` as `google_news.topic` in `POST /api/feeds/conversions`. One page.

post.summary: Turn a spoken question into text.
post.description: Rate limited by the `RL_AI` binding, and by a daily budget (`GET /api/users/self/usage`) answered with 429 and `Retry-After` until midnight UTC. Transcribed by Workers AI's Whisper, for asking with `POST /api/articles/{id}/answers`; nothing is kept.

get.summary: Sources other readers follow alongside the person's own.
get.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. Co-subscription, most shared first, leaving out sources the person follows already; at most ten, as one page. Follow one with `POST /api/feeds` and its `url`.

post.summary: Fetch every feed the person follows again now.
post.description: A refresh is not stored, so the result is the response and the answer is 200, not 201. Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding.

200.description: How many feeds there were and how many refreshed or failed.

post.summary: File several feeds under one section at once.
post.description: As NewsBlur moves a selection of feeds into a folder. Their other sections stay. Ids that are not the person's are skipped. A move is not stored, so the result is the response and the answer is 200. Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding.

section_id.description: One of the person's sections, or null for none.

post.summary: Stop following several feeds at once.
post.description: Ids that are not the person's are skipped. A removal is not stored, so the result is the response and the answer is 200. Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding.

get.summary: The VAPID public key a browser subscribes to pushes with.
get.description: Public. Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding.

get.summary: List the feeds trending across the app, or search them.
get.description: With `q`, a search of the sources anyone follows whose title or address holds it (NewsBlur's feed autocomplete), most followed first, as one page of RankedSource items saying whether the caller follows each; `order`, `window` and `cursor` are then refused. Without `q`, rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. Ranks sources across everyone, not only the ones the person follows, by distinct readers (`reads`), seconds spent (`read_time`) or new followers weighted by how recently they followed (`follows`, from a score of four) within the `window`, most first. Sources with no story in a year are left out.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Search text, from 2 to 200 characters.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: Required unless searching with `q`.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The opaque cursor from a previous page's `next`.

post.summary: Add a section to group feeds under on the front page.
post.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. Without a position the section goes after its siblings. A `parent_id` that is not one of the person's sections is a 400.

patch.summary: Rename, reorder or move a section under another.
patch.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. Only the members sent are changed. An id that cannot name a section is a 404.

200.description: The section as it is now.

delete.summary: Remove a section; its feeds stay, under no section, and the sections inside it move up to its parent.
delete.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. An id that cannot name a section is a 404. With `feeds=unfollow`, as deleting a NewsBlur folder does, the sections inside it go too, and so does every feed filed only inside them; a feed also filed elsewhere stays there.

get.summary: List the curated topics with their starter feeds.
get.description: The list is short and fixed, so it is always one page. Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding.

delete.description: Ends every session of the signed-in person on every device and clears this browser's cookie. Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding.
Clears the session cookie. Idempotent, and does not need a login, so signing out twice is fine. Rate limited by the `RL_AUTH` binding.

get.summary: List the classifiers that train the paper, newest first.
get.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding.

post.summary: Like or dislike stories by author, source, title phrase or tag.
post.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. Sending a kind and value already trained replaces its score and answers 200.

200.description: The classifier was there already; its score is now the one sent.

delete.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. An id that cannot name a classifier is a 404.

get.summary: List the archive searches the person keeps, newest first.
get.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding.

post.summary: Keep an archive search, optionally within one feed.
post.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. Saving the same words for the same feed again answers 200 with the search kept before. A `feed_id` that is not one of the person's feeds is a 400.

200.description: The same search was kept before.

delete.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. An id that cannot name a saved search is a 404.

get.summary: The person's listening player.
get.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. Someone who never listened gets the empty player.

put.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. Holds the playback rate, the story being read and how far in, and the queue and history.

post.summary: Mark many stories read at once.
post.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. As NewsBlur's mark-all, mark-feed and mark-stories read. The body names at least one member, each narrowing the rest; `before` as now marks every unread story in the person's feeds. Backs the mark-all, mark-above and mark-below shortcuts.

200.description: The stories now read. Named `article_ids` that are not stories in the person's feeds are left out; without `article_ids`, only the stories this request marked.

get.summary: Read what the person chose about clustering and the editor's note.
get.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. Defaults apply to whatever the person never changed.

patch.summary: Change some of the person's preferences.
patch.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. Members left out keep their value.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: The `ETag` of the preferences this change was made against.

200.description: All of the person's preferences, after the change.

post.summary: Note that a story was opened.
post.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. A read story is dimmed in its edition and left out of later ones. Noting it again answers 200.

201.description: The story is noted as read.

delete.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. The story is no longer dimmed, and later editions may show it again.

patch.summary: Note how long the person spent on a story they read.
patch.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. The longest time recorded stays; more than 1200 seconds counts as 1200. Trending ranks read time, long reads and good reads from it. A story with no read is a 404.

200.description: The read with the seconds now stored.

get.summary: List the rivers pinned to the person's front page.
get.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. The left column, then the right, each in order. A person pins at most 20, so the list is one page.

post.summary: Pin a river at a place, or change what the river there lists.
post.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. A river that lists something not the person's is a 400.

200.description: The river already at that place now lists this.

put.summary: Replace every pinned river at once.
put.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. A river that lists something not the person's, or two at one place, is a 400 and changes nothing.

200.description: The rivers as they are now.

delete.summary: Unpin a river; the ones below it in its column move up.
delete.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. A river that is not the person's is a 404.

get.summary: List the saved stories, newest save first.
get.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Only the stories matching these words as `GET /api/articles` matches `q`; a `tag:` term also matches the person's own tags on the save.

parameters.name: tag
parameters.description: Only the stories saved with this tag; empty for every one.

parameters.name: feed_id
parameters.description: Only the stories saved from this feed. A feed the person does not follow is a 400.

get.summary: List the tags on the saved stories, each with how many saves carry it.
get.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The tag, percent-encoded.

patch.summary: Rename a tag on every save carrying it.
patch.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. Renaming to a tag a save already has merges the two.

200.description: The tag as it is now.

delete.summary: Take a tag off every save; the saves stay.

204.description: No save carries the tag now.

get.summary: Count the saved stories from each of the person's feeds.
get.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. Feeds with no saves are left out.

post.summary: Save a story with tags, notes and highlights, keeping it after its edition is replaced.
post.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. The body may be left out. Saving a story again replaces its tags, and its notes and highlights when sent, and answers 200.

200.description: The story was saved already; its tags are now the ones sent.

post.summary: Share a story from the person's feeds, with an optional comment.
post.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. The body may be left out. Sharing a story again replaces its comment and answers 200.

200.description: The story was shared already; its comment is now the one sent.

204.description: The story is no longer shared.

get.summary: List the stories people shared, newest first.
get.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. Shares are public to everyone signed in, and name the sharer by id and name only.

parameters.name: user_id
parameters.description: Only these people's shares, repeated or comma separated (at most 100); everyone's when left out.

post.summary: Be told about new stories a classifier matches.
post.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. After each daily scrape, up to three new stories a rule matches are sent by each channel; a story goes out once even when several feeds or rules find it. A phrase matches case-insensitively (an author exactly); with `is_regex` the value is a case-insensitive regular expression over the title, author, text or address, and a pattern that could backtrack without end (a repeated group that repeats, or a back-reference) is refused. Nobody away for more than 90 days is notified.

put.summary: Be told about new stories in one of your feeds.
put.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. After each daily scrape, up to three new stories a feed are sent by each channel. `unread` sends any story not disliked; `focus` only liked ones. Email goes to the account's own address, at most 25 a day, once Email Sending is set up. `webhook` delivers a `story` event to the webhooks that ask for it. To stop, DELETE rather than sending no channels.

delete.summary: Stop being told about new stories in a feed.

post.summary: Notify this browser when the day's issue is ready.
post.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. The body is what the browser's `PushSubscription.toJSON()` gives. Posting an endpoint already known moves it to the caller with the keys sent and answers 200.

200.description: The endpoint was known; it is now the caller's.

204.description: The browser will no longer be notified.

get.summary: Today's Ask AI and assistant budgets.
get.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. Budgets reset at midnight UTC; cached answers do not count.

post.summary: Make a token a feed reader can fetch `/feed.xml` with.
post.description: Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. The answer carries the `token` and its `feed_url` once; only a hash is kept. `/feed.xml?token=` serves Atom for the saved stories (optionally one tag), one section, or the whole edition.

204.description: The token no longer opens its feed.

post.summary: Tell an https address whenever the person saves or likes a story, or a notifying feed has a new one.
post.description:
Rate limited by the `RL_API` binding. The answer carries the `secret` once; it is never shown again.

Each delivery is a `POST` of `{event, occurred_at, data}` as JSON, where `data` is the save, the classifier, or (for `story`) the new story with its feed. IFTTT's Webhooks service can receive these. It carries `Webhook-Timestamp` (seconds since the epoch) and `Webhook-Signature: sha256=<hex>`, the HMAC-SHA256 of `<timestamp>.<body>` under the secret. Redirects are not followed.

edition.description: The day the article was scraped. Every edition is kept.

TrendingArticle.description: An article in a list. Ranked by a trending order, it carries its count in the window; only the count, never who. `read_count` comes with `reads`, `long_reads` and `good_reads`, `save_count` with `saves`, and `read_seconds` with `read_time`.

next.description: The following page. Absent on the last page.

type.description: A relative URI naming the kind of problem.

body_text.description: The readable text of the article's page, blocks separated by a blank line. Absent when the page was not fetched or held no text.

original_summary.description: The summary the story first had, when a later fetch of its feed changed it; `summary` is the latest. Absent when it never changed.

followed.description: Whether the person follows the story's source; follow it with `POST /api/feeds`.

section_ids.description: The sections whose feeds the edition prints; empty prints every feed.

query.description: Only stories whose title, summary or text holds every word.

tag.description: Only stories the person saved under this tag.

match.description: `title` when the headlines match, `related` when only the meaning does.

read.description: Whether the person has read this copy.

score.description: The person's training on this copy; -2 is a strong dislike.

image.description: With the expanded preview, the copy's picture.

excerpt.description: With the expanded preview, the copy's opening.

also_covered_by.description: The other sources that covered the same story, which print once.

covered_by.description: The other copies of the story folded into this one.

stories.description: The desk's stories in print order.

briefing.description: The editor's note on the top stories, when one was written.

briefing_stories.description: The stories the note covers, in the order it covers them, and why each was picked.

sections.description: The paper's sections in print order; the desks filed under no section come first, in one with no name.

title.description: Such as "Morning Daily Briefing — Sunday, November 1, 2026".

local_date.description: The day on the person's own clock the briefing is for.

period_start.description: The start of the window of stories it read.

next.description: The following page. Absent on the last page.

Question.description: Exactly one of `question_id` (a preset) and `question` (the reader's own).

model.description: The Workers AI model that answers.

thinking.description: Answer with a model that reasons first; its reasoning is left out of the answer.

history.description: The earlier turns a follow-up builds on. A preset with history is not cached.

question_id.description: The preset asked, when it was one.

cached.description: Whether the answer was given before and served again; a cached answer does not count against the budget.

title.description: The first question, cut to 50 characters.

updated_at.description: When the last turn was added.

href.description: The page that shows the article, `/article/{article_id}`.

to.description: One to ten addresses, as a list or one string separated by commas or spaces.

comment.description: The sender's note, shown above the story.

from_name.description: The name the email goes out under, instead of the account's.

copy_me.description: Whether the sender gets a copy.

Icon.description: A custom icon, as NewsBlur has for folders and feeds.

data.description: The emoji (at most 8 characters), the icon's name in its set (lowercase letters, digits and hyphens), or a `data:image/png;base64,` URL of at most 100000 characters.

set.description: Only for a preset icon; lucide when not given.

AutoMarkReadDays.description: After how many days stories count as read and drop out of the reader's paper. 0 never marks them read; absent (or null when changing) inherits from the section above, else never.

name.description: The element's name as written, with any prefix (sy:updatePeriod, atom:link).

title.description: The person's own name for the feed, else the feed's.

muted.description: A muted feed stays followed but is left out of the paper. False again once a timed mute runs out.

muted_until.description: When a timed mute runs out; absent when the feed is not muted for a time.

position.description: Where the feed sits in the person's order; ties go by when it was followed.

section_ids.description: Every section the feed is filed in, the one it prints under (`section_id`) first. A feed can sit in several, as in several NewsBlur folders; the paper prints it once.

section_id.description: The section the feed is filed under; absent when none.

format.description: The kind of feed, as its document declares; absent until fetched.

site_url.description: The site the feed belongs to.

icon.description: The feed's own image, else the site's favicon.

updated_at.description: When the feed says it last changed.

update_minutes.description: How often the feed says it changes (sy:updatePeriod and sy:updateFrequency, else ttl).

metadata.description: Every element of the feed's header (the RSS or RDF channel, or the Atom feed, without its items), exactly as the feed gives it. Empty until fetched.

title.description: The person's own name for the feed; null or blank goes back to the feed's own.

url.description: A new address for the feed, the way out of a feed that moved. The person follows that address in its place; 409 when they already follow it.

muted.description: False also forgets any time a mute was to run out.

muted_until.description: When the mute runs out, or null to mute for good.

section_id.description: One of the person's sections to print under, or null for none. The feed's other sections stay. Send either this or `section_ids`.

section_ids.description: Every section to file the feed in, replacing the old ones; it prints under the first. An empty list files it nowhere.

custom_icon.description: The person's own icon for the feed, or null for the feed's own.

rejected.description: Entries that could not be followed, with why.

last_fetched_at.description: Absent when the feed has not been fetched yet.

last_error.description: Why the last fetch failed; absent when it did not.

fail_count.description: Fetches that failed in a row.

update_minutes.description: Minutes the feed asks to be left between fetches, when it says.

active_subscribers.description: Those of them who have it unmuted.

stories_last_month.description: Stories first seen in the last 30 days.

stories_per_month.description: Stories per month, newest first, at most 12 months.

stories_per_weekday.description: Stories by day of the week, 0 being Sunday.

stories_per_hour.description: Stories by hour of the day (UTC) they were published.

next_fetch_at.description: When the feed may be fetched again after failures; absent when it is due.

archive_count.description: Stories whose full text has been kept.

classifier_counts.description: The caller's unread stories in the feed (the newest 300) by how their training scores them, as NewsBlur's per-feed focus, neutral and hidden counts.

neutral.description: Stories training neither likes nor dislikes.

last_load_time_ms.description: How long the last timed fetch took.

fetch_history.description: The latest fetches, newest first, at most 25.

stories_per_day.description: Stories per edition day, newest first, at most 14 days.

followers.description: How many people who share a source with the caller follow this one.

followed.description: Whether the person asking follows it.

url.description: A newsletter, blog, YouTube channel or playlist, or feed address.

google_news.description: A search (`query`) or a topic (`topic`, from `GET /api/news/topics`).

vapid_public_key.description: The uncompressed P-256 public key, base64url.

Source.description: A feed trending across the app. Only counts are shown, never who; a source shows only once two or more people follow it and are behind its count. Following one is `POST /api/feeds` with its `url`.

read_count.description: With `order=reads`, the distinct readers in the window.

read_seconds.description: With `order=read_time`, the seconds spent in the window.

follow_score.description: With `order=follows`, the people who started following in the window, each weighted down the longer ago they followed (NewsBlur's decay tables); a source needs four.

parent_id.description: One of the person's sections to nest under, or null for the top level. The section itself, or one inside it, is refused with 400.

position.description: Sections go down the front page in this order, among the sections that share a parent.

parent_id.description: The section this one nests under; absent at the top level. A nested section's feeds print under a heading that names the sections it is in, and an edition that prints a section prints the sections inside it too.

ClassifierKind.description: What a classifier matches, as NewsBlur's classifiers. The story's own (title, author, tag, text, url) decide; only when none of them match do the feed and site (`feed`, `source`) ones count.

ClassifierScore.description: Liked stories are promoted toward the lead and features; disliked ones are hidden at the reader's intelligence level (see the preferences). A super dislike beats any like, and a like beats a dislike.

value.description: What to match, ignoring case. A phrase in the title (matched at the start of a word), the author, a tag, a phrase in the text, part of the story's address, a feed id, or the site a story is from.

is_regex.description: The value is a regular expression (title, author, text or url).

feed_id.description: The classifier applies only to this feed's stories. Absent, with no `section_id`, it applies everywhere.

section_id.description: The classifier applies only to the stories of this section's feeds.

ClassifierInput.description: A `prompt` classifier's value is up to 1000 characters the AI judges each story against, and its score is like (focus) or dislike (hidden). A regular expression may not nest quantifiers or refer back to a group.

feed_id.description: Scope the classifier to one of the person's feeds.

is_regex.description: Treat the value as a regular expression; only for title, author, text and url.

section_id.description: Scope the classifier to one of the person's sections. Not with `feed_id`.

query.description: The words searched for, as `q` of `GET /api/articles`.

feed_id.description: The one feed searched within. Absent when every feed is searched.

articles.description: The `GET /api/articles` address that runs this search.

next.description: The following page. Absent on the last page.

feed_ids.description: Only these feeds of the person's.

section_id.description: Only the feeds filed under this section of the person's.

before.description: Only stories published before this time.

after.description: Only stories published after this time.

enabled.description: Write an editor's note on each day's paper.

read_filter.description: `focus` covers only stories the person trained the paper to like.

day.description: The weekday a weekly briefing comes on.

sources.description: `all`, or `section:{id}` for one of the person's sections and those nested in it.

include_read.description: Cover stories the person already read.

model.description: The Workers AI model that writes the note; absent for the server's default.

sections.description: Each section on or off. Top stories is always on; a keyword section is on only with its prompt.

prompts.description: Keyword prompts, one per section of the person's own (`custom_1` to `custom_5`).

Intelligence.description: How much of the paper training lets through, as NewsBlur's intelligence levels. Focus shows only liked stories, unread all but disliked ones, all every story with disliked ones last.

story_clustering.description: Print the same story from several sources once. Clusters are only found while the server's Vectorize index is bound.

cluster_mode.description: `title` folds only copies whose headlines match; `related` also folds those that mean the same.

cluster_mark_read.description: Opening one copy of a story marks its other copies read.

cluster_preview_style.description: `expanded` shows each copy with its picture and opening.

timezone.description: The person's IANA time zone, whose clock briefings keep.

mark_read_on_open.description: Opening a story marks it read.

auto_mark_read_days.description: Days after which stories count as read when no feed or section says (0 never).

mark_read_on_scroll.description: Stories scrolled past are marked read, as NewsBlur's mark-read-on-scroll.

River.description: A story list pinned to the left or right column of the front page.

river_id.description: What it lists. `all` (every feed), `saves`, or `feed:`, `section:`, `search:` or `edition:` and one of the person's own ids.

items.description: No two at the same side and position.

notes.description: The person's own note on the story; absent when none.

highlights.description: Passages the person marked; absent when none.

count.description: How many saves carry the tag.

notes.description: Left out keeps the notes; null or blank clears them.

comments.description: What the sharer said about the story; absent when nothing.

sharer.description: Who shared it, by id and name, never by email.

kind.description: With `prompt`, the value is the reader's own words and Workers AI judges each new story in scope against them, each question counting against the daily AI classifier budget.

is_regex.description: Only for title, author, text and url.

feed_id.description: Required with `feed`, and only allowed with it.

section_id.description: Required with `section`, and only allowed with it.

expirationTime.description: As the browser names it; ignored.

scope.description: `highlights` lists the saved stories the person highlighted passages in, each entry quoting the passages and then their note.

tag.description: Only with `saves`, narrowing the feed to stories with this tag.

section_id.description: Required with `section`, and only allowed with it.

search_id.description: Required with `search`, and only allowed with it. The feed lists what the saved search finds, newest first.

filter.description: For a section or edition feed, `unread` leaves out disliked stories and `focus` keeps only liked ones. A saves, search or highlights feed is always `all`.

token.description: Only in the answer that made the token.

feed_url.description: The `/feed.xml` address the token opens. Only in the answer that made the token.

secret.description: Signs each delivery. Only in the answer that made the webhook.

BadRequest.description: The request is not valid. `errors` names the failing fields.

Unauthorized.description: Nobody is signed in, or the session has been ended.

TooManyRequests.description: The platform rate limit was reached.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before trying again.

NotFound.description: There is no such resource for this person.

Forbidden.description: The request came from another site.

UnsupportedMediaType.description: The request body is not JSON.

BadGateway.description: The model behind the assistant could not answer.

ServiceUnavailable.description: The feature is not set up on this server.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before trying again.

PreconditionFailed.description: `If-Match` names a version that is no longer current.

Cursor.name: cursor
Cursor.description: The opaque cursor from a page's `next` link.

session.name: broadsheet_session
session.description: The signed session cookie that signing in with Google at `/auth/login` sets, sent as a `Cookie: broadsheet_session=<value>` header. Any signed-in person can call every operation with it, except that deciding on feed recommendations (`PATCH /api/feeds/recommendations/{id}`) and listing the `pending` and `declined` ones (`GET /api/feeds/recommendations?status=`) need the curator capability. The operator grants it to an account by listing its email in the `CURATOR_EMAILS` variable, so a test account can be given it the same way. There is no other operator or administrator role in this contract.
